mechanism_narrative: Sustained week-on-week improvement in RETAIL_REC (from -66.4% to -57.6% over four weeks) reflects a monotonic recovery trend. This trend continues linearly into the next four weeks, producing net positive direction in mean RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 8.8 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has recovered sharply from -59.1% to -37.3% (21.8 point gain), signaling outdoor activity resumption. This outdoor-to-retail substitution effect reverses as weather stabilizes and indoor retail becomes more attractive, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 15 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 21.8 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to baseline faster than PARKS over the next 14 days, or PARKS mobility reverses by more than 10 points.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains elevated relative to baseline (-25.6% vs -66.4% RETAIL_REC), indicating essential-goods shopping dominates. Consumers accumulating essential supplies reduce retail discretionary visits. If GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes above -20%, retail recovery stalls due to budget reallocation away from recreation.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above -25% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves by more than 5 percentage points over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM stays above -25%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has declined only 5 percentage points over four weeks (from -59.1% to -54.1%), indicating persistent mobility restrictions. When TRANSIT falls below -50%, capacity constraints on public transport limit retail cluster access. RETAIL_REC remains suppressed as long as TRANSIT stays below -50%.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -50% for all four weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -54.1% across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 10 percentage points over the next 28 days while TRANSIT remains below -50%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT co-move (both declining ~5 points over four weeks), indicating coordinated return-to-work. When both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve simultaneously, commuting infrastructure enables retail cluster visits. Joint improvement in both proxies over the next week triggers retail recovery within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve by >3 percentage points in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days of simultaneous WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improvement, or either series reverses by >5 points.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 18.4% to 14.9% (3.5 point drop), indicating reduced home-confinement. When RESIDENTIAL falls below 16%, consumers spend more time outside homes. Combined with PARKS recovery, this signals outdoor-to-retail substitution. RETAIL_REC rises when both RESIDENTIAL declines and PARKS remains elevated.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 16% AND PARKS remains above -40%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase by at least 5 percentage points over the next 14 days when RESIDENTIAL is below 16% and PARKS above -40%.

mechanism_narrative: March 15 marks early spring in Lombardy. Seasonal warming and Easter holiday proximity (April 4, 2021) drive anticipatory retail spending. This seasonal effect is regime-independent and produces RETAIL_REC gains regardless of restriction status, with a one-week lag before consumer behavior shifts.
evidence_refs: fact:Decision date is March 15, 2021, pre-Easter period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not show week-on-week improvement in the week of March 22-28, 2021, or Easter holiday effect does not materialize by April 4.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility at -49.7% indicates partial workplace reopening. When WORKPLACES improves above -45%, it signals policy relaxation. This policy signal cascades to RETAIL_REC within four weeks as consumer confidence recovers. The mechanism requires sustained WORKPLACES improvement (no reversal >5 points) to maintain retail momentum.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves above -45% and sustains for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 3.6 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the last 28-day mean, or WORKPLACES reverses below -50% before week two.
